title: Karpathy on the cognitive core
summary: Karpathy proposes retaining general problem-solving strategies while relying more on looking up detailed knowledge. Around 56:20 he explains why reducing memorized facts interests him.
action: Compare Gemma choosing a question from familiar API examples with the same decision expressed as anonymous symbols.
caveat: A conjecture from an interview. Renaming symbols changes the input representation and cannot isolate a mechanism in model weights.

title: Ambig-SWE: Interactive Agents to Overcome Underspecificity in Software Engineering
summary: The authors distinguish recognizing missing requirements, asking a targeted question and using the answer.
action: Log wasted questions and whether the final choice contradicts an answer the agent already received.
caveat: PatchQuestions supplies a fixed menu and a reliable oracle. Free-form clarification involves additional skills.

title: Ask or Assume? Uncertainty-Aware Clarification-Seeking in Coding Agents
summary: The authors separate uncertainty detection from execution in a study of underspecified repository issues. Their scaffold spends clarification effort selectively.
action: Allow an early final choice and report accuracy alongside questions actually used.
caveat: Their repository resolution rate and our held-out agreement have different denominators and success criteria.

title: SWE-Clar: Can Coding Agents Clarify Incomplete Client Requirements and Deliver Greenfield Software?
summary: SWE-Clar separates clarification conversations from implementation and evaluates both against client requirements.
action: Keep the transcript and held-out test outcome as separate evidence for each episode.
caveat: Greenfield commissions and finite API configuration choices measure different tasks. This is a preprint.

title: Interactive Patch Filtering as Debugging Aid
authors: Jingjing Liang, Ruyi Ji, Jiajun Jiang, Shurui Zhou, Yiling Lou, Yingfei Xiong, Gang Huang
summary: InPaFer helps developers review generated patches by asking questions that eliminate groups of incorrect patches. It is direct prior art for interactive patch filtering.
action: Read the filtering criteria and user-study design. Explain precisely what PatchQuestions adds through exact finite evaluation and probe-vocabulary experiments.
caveat: Asking developers distinguishing questions is already established. The 2020 arXiv draft has a different author list from the 2021 published paper.
verification: Author publication page and author-hosted paper; metadata and abstract checked.

title: Human-In-The-Loop Automatic Program Repair
authors: Marcel Böhme, Charaka Geethal, Van-Thuan Pham
summary: LEARN2FIX uses a limited budget of user labels to learn when a program exhibits a bug, then uses the learned oracle to support repair.
action: Add a related-work comparison covering query budgets, oracle availability, and noisy or imperfect labels.
caveat: Its learned bug oracle and numeric-input setting differ from selecting among a fixed candidate behavior matrix.
verification: arXiv metadata, abstract and ICST acceptance note checked.

title: Identifying Test-Suite-Overfitted Patches through Test Case Generation
summary: DiffTGen generates inputs that expose semantic differences and helps detect patches that pass existing tests while failing to repair the underlying behavior.
action: Compare informative probe generation with fixed-pool question selection, and document which trusted reference supplies the expected outputs.
caveat: Behavioral differences expose uncertainty. They require an oracle before they establish correctness.
verification: Official ISSTA program and abstract checked.

title: Test-based Patch Clustering for Automatically-Generated Patches Assessment
authors: Matias Martinez, Maria Kechagia, Anjana Perera, Justyna Petke, Federica Sarro, Aldeida Aleti
summary: xTestCluster groups plausible patches according to their behavior on generated tests, reducing the set of patches a developer needs to inspect.
action: Include behavioral clustering as a baseline or explicitly position the current behavior partitions relative to it.
caveat: The published evaluation studies Java APR patches. PatchQuestions currently studies curated Python configurations.
verification: Updated arXiv metadata, abstract and journal DOI checked.

title: Automated Patch Assessment for Program Repair at Scale
authors: He Ye, Matias Martinez, Martin Monperrus
summary: This study assesses patches by generating tests whose expected behavior comes from a human-written reference patch, using Random Testing with Ground Truth.
action: Make the simulated oracle assumption explicit and keep reference outputs isolated from candidate and probe generation.
caveat: Access to a correct reference is a strong evaluation assumption that deployment may not satisfy.
verification: Publisher authors, publication date and abstract checked.

title: CodeMonkeys: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Software Engineering
authors: Ryan Ehrlich, Bradley Brown, Jordan Juravsky, Ronald Clark, Christopher Ré, Azalia Mirhoseini
summary: CodeMonkeys generates multiple edit trajectories and selects among candidates using model-generated tests and a dedicated selection trajectory.
action: Use its candidate-selection setting to motivate a small, controlled Gemma-generated patch study and account for test-generation cost.
caveat: Its reported scores and spend belong to its own models, harness and benchmark. They are not evidence for PatchQuestions.
verification: Primary arXiv authors, date and abstract checked.

title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
authors: Chunqiu Steven Xia, Yinlin Deng, Soren Dunn, Lingming Zhang
summary: Agentless separates repository localization, repair and validation into a comparatively simple workflow instead of allowing unconstrained action planning.
action: Build a minimal candidate/probe/selection pipeline first and compare the proposed selection method under a fixed scaffold.
caveat: The original results use a particular SWE-bench subset and model configuration. Current leaderboard ranks are outside this summary.
verification: Primary arXiv title, authors, date and abstract checked.

title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
authors: John Yang, Carlos E. Jimenez, Alexander Wettig, Kilian Lieret, Shunyu Yao, Karthik Narasimhan, Ofir Press
summary: SWE-agent investigates how interfaces for repository navigation, file editing and test execution affect an agent's software-engineering performance.
action: Give the experimental model a small, explicit query/pick interface and log invalid actions and recovery attempts.
caveat: A good interface can alter outcomes, so keep it identical across policies when testing question-selection benefits.
verification: Primary arXiv abstract and official project documentation checked.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
authors: Carlos E. Jimenez, John Yang, Alexander Wettig, Shunyu Yao, Kexin Pei, Ofir Press, Karthik Narasimhan
summary: SWE-bench evaluates edits for real repository issues by executing tests on the patched codebase.
action: Add a tightly scoped real-issue pilot after the synthetic resource is stable, with failing and regression tests isolated from the model.
caveat: Curated API configuration recovery measures a narrower capability than repository-level repair.
verification: Primary arXiv metadata and abstract checked.

title: SWE-bench Verified
summary: Verified is a human-validated subset of 500 SWE-bench instances intended to improve the reliability of task descriptions and tests.
action: Use a small predefined subset if repository experiments fit the schedule. Record instance identifiers before tuning.
caveat: The 500 instances are the full subset, not a claim that this project has evaluated them.
verification: Official benchmark overview checked.

title: SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks?
summary: SWE-Bench Pro targets longer and more complex repository tasks across a wider set of maintained projects.
action: Use it to delimit claims and identify future transfer targets after the paper deadline.
caveat: Its long-horizon tasks can exceed the available one-week budget. Reported historical scores do not describe current frontier performance.
verification: Primary arXiv metadata and abstract checked.

title: Query by Committee
authors: H. Sebastian Seung, Manfred Opper, Haim Sompolinsky
summary: Query by committee selects examples where competing hypotheses disagree, providing a foundational connection to informative probe selection.
action: Cite it when introducing disagreement and entropy baselines. Define how candidate priors and duplicated candidates affect the committee.
caveat: Disagreement-based selection is a foundational method. A new benchmark must establish its additional contribution.
verification: Author-affiliated university publication record and abstract checked.

title: Active Learning Literature Survey
summary: This survey organizes active-learning settings and query strategies for learning from a constrained labeling budget.
action: Specify whether the experiment chooses from a fixed pool or synthesizes queries, and separate label count from labeling effort.
caveat: A survey supplies conceptual framing rather than a direct software-repair evaluation baseline.
verification: University report record and author publications checked.

title: The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey
authors: Earl T. Barr, Mark Harman, Phil McMinn, Muzammil Shahbaz, Shin Yoo
summary: The test-oracle problem is deciding whether observed behavior is correct. The survey covers specifications, contracts, metamorphic relations and human judgments.
action: State who provides expected outputs in every experiment and add an abstain option where no trusted label exists.
caveat: Candidate consensus cannot itself establish correctness. Human labels also have costs and errors.
verification: Author institution's metadata and abstract checked.

title: Metamorphic Testing: A Review of Challenges and Opportunities
authors: Tsong Yueh Chen, Fei-Ching Kuo, Huai Liu, Pak-Lok Poon, Dave Towey, T. H. Tse, Zhi Quan Zhou
summary: Metamorphic testing checks necessary relationships between multiple executions when exact expected outputs are difficult to obtain.
action: Explore a small set of justified API relations as an alternative or complement to asking for complete output values.
caveat: Each relation needs domain justification. A plausible but invalid relation can wrongly reject a correct candidate.
verification: Author-hosted publication metadata and abstract checked.

title: Pynguin: Automated Unit Test Generation for Python
summary: Pynguin is an extensible Python regression-test generator that uses coverage-oriented automated generation.
action: If integration is quick, compare a generated probe pool with the handcrafted pool while keeping the selection policy fixed.
caveat: Coverage-oriented regression tests can preserve current behavior, including existing bugs, unless their oracle is independently validated.
verification: Primary arXiv metadata, abstract and DOI checked.

title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
authors: Jiawei Liu, Chunqiu Steven Xia, Yuyao Wang, Lingming Zhang
summary: EvalPlus expands code-generation evaluation tests using LLM-generated seeds and mutation-based inputs, revealing mistakes missed by smaller suites.
action: Expand held-out edge cases independently of probe tuning and preserve the original fixed suite for comparison.
caveat: More tests still approximate semantic correctness. Test generation must avoid leaking the hidden reference to the policy.
verification: Primary arXiv metadata and abstract checked.

title: Automated Unit Test Improvement using Large Language Models at Meta
authors: Nadia Alshahwan, Jubin Chheda, Anastasia Finegenova, Beliz Gokkaya, Mark Harman, Inna Harper, Alexandru Marginean, Shubho Sengupta, Eddy Wang
summary: TestGen-LLM improves human-written tests and filters generated tests for successful builds, reliable execution and measurable improvement.
action: Validate model-generated probes before counting them. Log syntax failures, nondeterminism and measurable behavioral distinctions separately.
caveat: Coverage gains alone do not establish that a generated assertion represents the intended contract.
verification: Primary arXiv metadata and abstract checked.

title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
summary: The Gemma team describes the open-weight family, efficiency decisions, reasoning behavior and evaluation in its technical report.
action: Record the exact model artifact and revision used in experiments. Cite the model report without transferring family-level claims to our result.
caveat: The competition-supported model identifier must be verified against Kaggle's current harness rather than inferred from a family overview.
verification: Primary arXiv author listing, date and abstract checked.

title: Google — The Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track
summary: The paper track accepts original unpublished research in a Kaggle Writeup, capped at 3,000 words. Judging equally weights novelty, quality, relevance, verifiability and clarity.
action: Submit the final Writeup before 12 November 2026, 23:59 UTC (13 November, 04:59 Pakistan time). A saved draft must still be submitted.
caveat: Source retrieval confirmed the official requirements; competition pages can be updated, so recheck the live page before submitting.
verification: Official Kaggle indexed overview checked; live page extraction unavailable through search open.

title: Google — The Gemma 4 Developer Agent Competition
summary: The main track evaluates repository patches through validation tests and defines the supported model variant and agent harness. It is a separate entry from the paper track.
action: Keep research-adviser API use separate from the offline competition agent. Verify exact model and harness constraints before running a main-track submission.
caveat: Participation in the main track is optional for the paper. Graph and embedding data are encouraged for papers, with no mandatory use stated in the overview.
verification: Official Kaggle indexed main overview checked.

title: Building effective agents
summary: Anthropic describes simple composable agent patterns and advises adding complexity when evaluation supports the tradeoff.
action: Keep this week's experiment pipeline small, inspectable and bounded by measurable stop conditions.
caveat: Engineering guidance is experiential rather than a controlled PatchQuestions result. The article itself notes that tooling has changed since publication.
verification: Official article title, date and relevant guidance checked.

title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
summary: The essay distinguishes tasks, trials, graders, transcripts and outcomes, and discusses combining deterministic and calibrated human or model grading.
action: Store full trial provenance and actual graded outcomes. Repeat stochastic model trials instead of treating one successful transcript as a stable estimate.
caveat: Use model judges for qualitative review only when calibrated. Functional correctness here should remain executable and reference-based.
verification: Official article date, definitions and grader guidance checked.

title: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals
summary: Controlled internal experiments show that resource allocation and enforcement can change measured agentic benchmark performance.
action: Record Python version, hardware, resource limits, API latency, concurrency and infrastructure failures for each model experiment.
caveat: Its measured effect sizes concern its own setups. They motivate controls rather than predict an effect size for our benchmark.
verification: Official report date, experimental description and recommendations checked.

title: Writing effective tools for agents — with agents
summary: This essay recommends explicit tool boundaries, informative responses and evaluation-driven refinement of the tools agents use.
action: Validate the query/pick JSON protocol, provide actionable error messages and capture whether failures came from selection reasoning or tool misuse.
caveat: A provider's engineering recommendations need project-specific validation.
verification: Official engineering article and research mirror checked.

title: Gemma 4: Byte for byte, the most capable open models
summary: Google introduces the Gemma 4 family with an emphasis on reasoning, agentic workflows and local deployment.
action: Use the announcement for project context and follow its official model links when choosing an experiment artifact.
caveat: Vendor capability and ranking statements are time-specific promotional claims. Record the actual artifact and measured local results.
verification: Official Google announcement authors, date and product framing checked.

title: NeurIPS Hacker Cup AI: SWEAgent
authors: Kilian Lieret; hosted by Weights & Biases
summary: A researcher-led practical introduction to SWE-agent setup, operation and customization, linked from the project's official documentation.
action: Watch the setup and configuration portions when implementing the minimal repository pilot.
caveat: Video metadata and official documentation link were verified. The video was not watched in full, and commands may have changed.
verification: YouTube indexed metadata and official SWE-agent documentation cross-link checked; direct video fetch unavailable.

title: SWE-agent project introduction
summary: The SWE-agent maintainers link this video as the project's quick introduction to the software-engineering agent and its interface.
action: Use it for a quick conceptual overview before reading the paper and building the experiment harness.
caveat: The title here describes its role in the official documentation. Exact video title and publication day were not independently retrieved.
verification: The exact video ID was verified in official SWE-agent documentation. Direct YouTube metadata retrieval failed.

title: Towards Autonomous Language Model Systems
summary: This researcher talk covers the motivation behind SWE-bench and SWE-agent and discusses autonomous software-engineering systems.
action: Use the event abstract as researcher perspective on why realistic end-to-end evaluations matter.
caveat: The official event page was verified. A playable recording was not located, so this entry links to the talk page.
verification: MIT CSAIL event date, speaker and abstract checked.

title: SWE-Bench Pro Verified: A Reliable Benchmark for Software Engineering Agents
authors: Pujun Zheng, Zixin Shang, Shufan Jiang, Wenhui Tian, Dongsheng Zhu, Zerun Ma, Dingbo Yuan, Qi Zhang
summary: This preprint analyzes leakage and task-quality problems in SWE-Bench Pro and introduces safeguards and task refinements.
action: Audit candidate generation and evaluation for access to gold outputs, hidden tests and target identifiers before any Gemma comparison.
caveat: This is a recent preprint. Its findings concern SWE-Bench Pro and should guide an audit rather than be assumed to apply identically here.
verification: Primary arXiv metadata and abstract checked.
